Since equivocations are not proven by the next proposer by putting them into the block, the safest strategy for the proposer is to include the txs of both ILs - and there is no punishment for equivocating. Is this intended? We're allowing 2x the actually needed networking traffic (=peers must forward 2 ILs per includer). I'd prefer only ever forwarding 1 IL per peer and instead put equivocations into the block (2x transactions_root + 2x signature) + a gossip topic for forwarding the equivocation proof. Under synchrony assumption, a proposer can ignore equivocating ILs, but for the satest strategy, the proposer can choose include only either of two evuiqocating ILs to produce IL-compliant payload. ILs are not put in the block because of free DA issue. right but that risks trusting in synchrony, and doesn't prevent that everyone can propagate 2 lists through the whole network? I'd say that the free DA isn't an issue as you can include sigs over the transactions_root of the IL instead of the full IL. Allowing up to 2 ILs is to deliver the equivocating evidence to other peers. It is an issue. You don't get any punishment for publishing any random bytes. yeah and it feels like a waste of resources to 2x networking in the worst-case just for equivocations? it would only be 2x 32 bytes + the sigs It affects forkchoice. It matters, isn't it? but yeah, thinking of leanXMSS which has much bigger sigs, it's not great. Today's situation I'd accept. No, it's random bytes of 8 KiB. yeah attesters would have to not enforce the ILs that the proposer could prove equivocated Maybe we're also making a bigger deal out of free DA than it actually is. With leanXMSS, if we have 2x 2.5 KIB sigs, I'd still accept it over the 2x in worst-case propagation, but would have to think about it more. 2x sounds particularly scary thinking of SPINCS txs and much larger ILs. to me it's pretty clear the right thing to do is not to have much bigger ILs to start with, just replace the IL sig by leanXMSS and accept you can only include a few (e.g., 2,3) leanSPHINCS txns per ILs at first imo we want to start conservative, by bounding the size and the gas of ILs so we're sure we don't impose a lot of network load yeah, I'm def for keeping them small. It implies that we would probably wait for allowing more pq-txs/IL only with aggregation supported. It's a separate topics though. I'm more thinking of the 2x networking worst-case bc we allow 2 ILs per peer to travel the whole network (forwarded by peers) instead of forwarding a much smaller equivocation proof. I get that just forwarding 2 is probably simpler (+having proposers include the txs of at least one, but better 2 ILs per peer) but it also 2x'es the worst-case bandwidth consumption. Any ideas for proving an equivocation succinctly? pre-pq: one would need to include 2 transactions_root, and could aggregate the bls sigs + 1b for the validator, in the block + propagate equivocation proofs instead of full ILs. That's 161 bytes. post-pq with xmss: you could aggregate the equivocation proof into the block's stark proof. The last recursion is now an ever growing demand of CPU on the proposer even before we started profiling PQ. It started with the proposer needing to aggregate attestations. Now we also need to aggregate attester slashings and ILs equivocations. Same with sync committee if we keep them. I suspect that IL equivocations can be just packed as concatenated XMSS sigs as they are only two. Same as with proposer slashings. Yeah agree, and i guess the sig merkle path would be the same for both, which helps too. But there can be 32 IL XMSS signatures in the worst case. I like the plan of keeping ILs small and keeping two ILs to spot equivocations, it's the most simple one for PQ FOCIL the way I'm thinking about it now is that we just replace the IL sig by leanXMSS, keep tight bounds on IL/txn size and gas, accept that only 1 or 2 PQ txns per IL would fit that way the footprint on the network stays very small (16 ILs are worth a bit more than 1 blob of gossip on the CL p2p size) when we get to an 8288 world with recursive mempool aggregation and a network that can handle recursive proofs natively then we can switch to post 8288 FOCIL, but that's further down the line yeah worst case scenario is 64KB and for an attacker with up to say 10% of the stake you won't expect more than 1 or 2 equivocations, giving 2 to 4KB of signatures. Given that the block is already half a megabyte anyway, I suspect concatenating the signatures is a better tradeoff than adding work to the recursion, but this should be benched It's not only broadcasting 2x but also 2x more work for builders in the worst-case. With frame txs, builders will have to include the tx_index where they tried inserting the transaction. Under asynchrony, builders may want to obey both ILs and they could have different txs (both ILs containing txs maxxing-out the VERIFY gas from eip-8141). This doubles work. And there could even be weird interactions with the transactions of equivocating ILs, which might be hard to test. My feeling is we should include the proofs in the block, have a gossip topic for forwarding equivocation proofs, and ignore every IL from an includer from whom we've already seen one and instead create an equivocation proof. Post-pq we can either aggregate the proof into the block's proof, or just keep including them in the block (which seems fine to). Independently from how we deal with equivocations, they shouldn't be ignored as done in `get_inclusion_list_transactions` in the specs: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/e3e2d0128458c2f56092bd459d3c5a85cdf80fcd/specs/heze/inclusion-list.md I think there are multiple ways to resolve this concern. 1) Make a bid includes a list of IL roots, instead of an IL bitlist, which is an idea brought up here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1210529202458071050/1567124235233656934. An attester can tell whether there was an equivocation when a bid has a different IL root than what it has for the same includer. With this approach, we can broadcast only one IL per includer, but equivocating ILs are enforced with the one that a builder chooses. However, I think it should be IL transactions roots and aggregated IL signatures. An attester will compute IL root and verify it against the aggregated signature. This is to prevent any forgery by builders. This aggregation should be benchmarked especially post-PQ. (cc <@1035747431461167125> for the IL roots in a bid design.) 2) Add an equivocation proof to the envelope. A naive approach is making a proof of two `SignedInclusionListHeader`. The proof varies depending on the design, e.g. aggregated signature. ``` class InclusionListHeader(Container): slot: Slot validator_index: ValidatorIndex dependent_root: Root transactions_root: Root class SignedInclusionListHeader(Container): message: InclusionListHeader signature: BLSSignature # leanXMSS signature post-PQ class InclusionListEquivocation(Container): signed_header_1: SignedInclusionListHeader signed_header_2: SignedInclusionListHeader ``` There maybe more options with different trade-offs. > have a gossip topic for forwarding equivocation proofs, and ignore every IL from an includer from whom we've already seen one and instead create an equivocation proof. While this would reduce the bandwidth consumption when there is any equivocation, it requires a careful examination on whether there will be any edge cases caused by the new gossip topic. Maybe it's worth to explore post-PQ but it also depends on the performance of our future p2p layer. Yeah including signed commitment to the IL in the bid seems like a nice solution too.

excerpts.author: jih2nn
excerpts.content:
I think there are multiple ways to resolve this concern.

1) Make a bid includes a list of IL roots, instead of an IL bitlist, which is an idea brought up here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1210529202458071050/1567124235233656934. An attester can tell whether there was an equivocation when a bid has a different IL root than what it has for the same includer. With this approach, we can broadcast only one IL per includer, but equivocating ILs are enforced with the one that a builder chooses.

However, I think it should be IL transactions roots and aggregated IL signatures. An attester will compute IL root and verify it against the aggregated signature. This is to prevent any forgery by builders. This aggregation should be benchmarked especially post-PQ. (cc <@1035747431461167125> for the IL roots in a bid design.)

2) Add an equivocation proof to the envelope. A naive approach is making a proof of two `SignedInclusionListHeader`. The proof varies depending on the design, e.g. aggregated signature.

```
class InclusionListHeader(Container):
    slot: Slot
    validator_index: ValidatorIndex
    dependent_root: Root
    transactions_root: Root

class SignedInclusionListHeader(Container):
    message: InclusionListHeader
    signature: BLSSignature # leanXMSS signature post-PQ

class InclusionListEquivocation(Container):
    signed_header_1: SignedInclusionListHeader
    signed_header_2: SignedInclusionListHeader
```

There maybe more options with different trade-offs.

excerpts.author: jih2nn
excerpts.content:
> have a gossip topic for forwarding equivocation proofs, and ignore every IL from an includer from whom we've already seen one and instead create an equivocation proof.

While this would reduce the bandwidth consumption when there is any equivocation, it requires a careful examination on whether there will be any edge cases caused by the new gossip topic. Maybe it's worth to explore post-PQ but it also depends on the performance of our future p2p layer.
